items.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attacks on security forces
items.summary: PARIS: France on Sunday launched an attempted murder probe after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during Paris protests, as footage of an officer in flames sparked outrage. The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. "Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said.

items.title: Mufti Menk visits Tun M, conveys condolences over Siti Hasmah's death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prominent preacher Mufti Menk visited Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today to convey his condolences over the death of the former prime minister's wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali. In a post on Threads, account holder Sulaiman an-Nuuri said Mufti Menk offered his condolences and referred to Dr Hasmah as "our mother". Referring to the story, Mufti Menk said Dr Hasmah's contributions and kindness to Malaysia and the ummah were immense, and prayed that Allah would grant her the highest level of paradise," the post said.

items.title: Woman falls from second floor of Tampoi flat after seizure
items.summary: Johor Baru North acting district police chief Superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said police received a report shortly after the incident. Azrol said police had identified four witnesses and would record their statements to assist with the investigation. Anyone with information can call 07-5563122, police said.

items.title: Woman's body found caught in fishing net buoy line in Sungai Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN: The body of an unidentified woman was found caught in a fishing net buoy line in Sungai Kuantan near Jalan Besar here today. Kuantan police chief assistant commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said police received information about the discovery from the public at 12.38pm. He said initial checks found the body of a woman believed to be in her 30s, wearing a red shirt and white shorts with black patterns.

items.title: Family dispute behind fight involving three men in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A family dispute is believed to have sparked a fight involving three men, including a senior citizen, outside a shop in Plentong. Seri Alam district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Sohaimi Ishak said the three men, aged between 27 and 60, had been arrested to assist investigations. "The three suspects have been remanded for three days until Nov 3 to assist investigations," he said.

items.title: Cops probe woman over incident involving two children at KL mall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating a woman accused of pushing and hitting two children at a shopping mall in the capital. Dang Wangi district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said police had detected the video and received an official report from the children's father. Ahmad Azwan said police viewed the incident seriously and were conducting an investigation.

items.title: Anwar announces RM1mil allocation to aid hawkers, small traders
items.summary: KAJANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has allocated RM1 million to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives to coordinate assistance for associations, hawkers and small traders to help boost their income. He said the allocation took into account the hundreds of thousands of hawkers, small traders and associations operating nationwide. The allocation comes amid the government's efforts to help low-income earners, including hawkers and small traders, increase their income.

items.title: Bukit Kuda rehab centre trespass: Cops investigate after group takes several inmates
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police are investigating a suspected trespassing incident involving a group who entered a private rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, near here, and removed several inmates without the management's permission. Klang Utara police chief assistant commissioner Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the centre's owner on Oct 28, claiming that a group of unidentified men and women had entered the premises and taken several inmates away. Ramsay advised the public against speculating on the case, saying this could affect public order and disrupt police investigations.

items.title: Burst tyre suspected in crash that killed couple in Batu Pahat
items.summary: Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the crash occurred while the MPV was travelling from Yong Peng towards Parit Sulong. The MPV driver, Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, and his wife, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, suffered serious injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene. His wife suffered serious head and internal injuries, and burns.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, Nov 1, 2026

items.title: 1,000 Titiwangsa residents receive Deepavali food baskets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,000 residents in the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency received food baskets ahead of Deepavali, which falls on Nov 8. Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the initiative was part of his regular efforts to spend time with and engage with the local community. During this weekend's break, I distributed Deepavali food baskets to 1,000 recipients in the Titiwangsa parliamentary constituency," he said in a Facebook post today.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN candidate pledges more jobs, affordable housing in Serkam
items.summary: JASIN: Creating more job opportunities and providing affordable housing for young people will be among Barisan Nasional candidate Datuk Azman Abdullah's priorities if he wins the Serkam seat in the Melaka election. Azman said his focus would be on strengthening youth development through the expansion of the Halal Hub industrial area in Serkam, particularly by creating employment opportunities linked to Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). He said the second phase of the industrial development, which was still under construction, could provide more job opportunities for local youths.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH candidate pledges to champion key issues in Machap Jaya
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan candidate for the Machap Jaya seat Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin has pledged to continue championing key issues involving infrastructure, welfare, the safety of children and women, road safety and the environment. She said her previous experience and service record were still remembered by some residents, motivating her to offer better services if given another opportunity to represent the constituency. Ginie also wants to focus on empowering women economically and creating more job opportunities and skills development programmes for young people.

items.title: At 81, grandfather of 35 earns PhD after mastering digital technology
items.summary: BACHOK: An 81-year-old grandfather of 35 has earned a PhD despite health challenges and the need to master computers and digital technology during his studies. Dr Abdul Ghani Muhamad graduated at Universiti Malaysia Kelantan's (UMK) convocation ceremony today. Ghani completed his PhD in Sufism and Tariqa studies in four years, on schedule.

items.title: Melaka polls: Candidates advised to respect media practitioners, says Fahmi
items.summary: MELAKA: Candidates contesting in the Melaka election have been advised to respect and appreciate the presence of media practitioners throughout the campaign period, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi also encouraged media practitioners to lodge complaints with the Malaysian Media Council if their content was plagiarised or used without permission. Meanwhile, Fahmi said that apart from the main media centre in Ayer Keroh, 39 National Information Dissemination Centres across Melaka had also been designated as media centres to facilitate media practitioners in carrying out their duties.

items.title: Online renewal for 10-year Malaysian passports starts tomorrow
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Passport renewal services through the MyOnline Passport system will offer a choice of five- or 10-year validity periods starting tomorrow. The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM), in a Facebook post, said the new facility allows applicants to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs. “This initiative provides greater flexibility and convenience for Malaysians to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs,” according to JIM.

items.title: Selangor schools open as usual tomorrow but parents may keep children home if concerned over haze, says state education dept
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 1 — All schools in Selangor will operate as usual tomorrow, according to the Selangor Education Department (JPN). In a statement today, the department urged all parties to continue prioritising the health and safety of students and school personnel in view of the current haze situation. “Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure, particularly those who are sensitive to haze conditions.

items.title: Selangor schools to operate as usual tomorrow despite haze
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: All schools in Selangor will operate as usual tomorrow, the Selangor Education Department (JPN) said. In a statement today, the department called on all parties to continue prioritising the health and safety of students and school personnel amid the current haze situation. "Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure, particularly those who are sensitive to haze conditions.

items.title: Iran army says any new war with US could be 'longer than previous conflict'
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran warned on Sunday that any new war with the United States could last longer than the previous conflict and that US President Donald Trump would not be the one to determine its duration. "A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. Iran's Defence Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi on Sunday warned of a "proportionate, decisive, and impactful response" to any attack on the country, according to state TV.

items.title: Melaka polls: MCMC won't interfere in online campaigns, will act only upon complaints
items.summary: MELAKA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by political parties contesting the Melaka election, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. Instead, he said the commission would actively monitor social media platforms and only initiate investigations or take action against posts upon receiving complaints from the public. "To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts related to campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms," he said when asked about the commission's online monitoring measures during the Melaka election, scheduled for Nov 14.

items.title: Over 400 people detained in drug raid on Jalan Sultan Ismail entertainment centre
items.summary: Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said all the arrests in the raid, which started around 2.30am, consisted of premises guards, workers and visitors, including four Bangladeshi nationals. “All those detained were brought to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters (IPD) for documentation and urine screening tests,” he said in a statement today. Meanwhile, in a separate raid, the police arrested eight individuals, including six foreigners, at another unlicensed entertainment centre on Jalan Tun Razak, around 2am earlier today.

items.title: Portuguese police clash with housing protesters, arrest 13
items.summary: LISBON: Riot police with dogs stormed protest camps in Lisbon and Porto early Sunday, charging demonstrators with batons, arresting 13 people and leaving dozens injured in the latest confrontation over Portugal's housing crisis. In Porto, police said three plain-clothes officers monitoring the protesters were assaulted after being spotted by a group. Police said they seized 69 tents in Lisbon and 30 in Porto.

items.title: Duyong incumbent: 'For five years, we have been on the ground'
items.summary: KOTA MELAKA: Duyong incumbent and Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem is banking on his five-year track record as he seeks re-election in Melaka. He said voters wanted a representative they knew, could approach and rely on to help resolve problems affecting the community. Mohd Noor Helmy said residents expected their elected representative to be visible and accessible, whether through social media or face-to-face engagement.

items.title: Kelantan Sultan urges graduates to become job creators, not job seekers
items.summary: BACHOK: University graduates should shift their focus from seeking employment to creating job opportunities by harnessing artificial intelligence (AI) and the digital economy, which are increasingly transforming the conventional employment landscape. Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V said Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) graduates, in particular, should view these changes as opportunities to venture into entrepreneurship, develop new business models and create jobs. His Royal Highness said the entrepreneurial values instilled at UMK should encourage graduates not merely to become job seekers, but also to become architects of opportunities and job creators.

items.title: Man, 42, dies after collapsing during running event in Putrajaya
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — A 42-year-old man died while participating in a running event here early this morning. Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said the victim was reported to have collapsed while participating in the event before being taken to the Putrajaya Hospital’s emergency department at around 6.52am. “The Putrajaya Hospital authorities tried to resuscitate the victim, but their efforts were unsuccessful and the victim was pronounced dead at 6.54am.

items.title: Guar Chempedak assemblyman, son injured after SUV overturns in Yan crash
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 1 — Guar Chempedak state assemblyman Abdul Ghafar Saad and his son sustained minor injuries after the sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in collided with a car in Ulu Sedaka, near Yan, yesterday. Yan deputy district police chief DSP Aikap Dunding said police received information about the accident, which happened in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Ulu Sedaka, at 8.41am. He said the Proton X50 SUV was driven by the 32-year-old son of the Guar Chempedak assemblyman, while Abdul Ghafar was a passenger in the vehicle.

items.title: Sell achievements, not slander: Asyraf Wajdi outlines BN's Melaka election strategy
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) campaign machinery has been reminded to focus on the coalition's track record and policy offers to the people during the Melaka election campaign, rather than resorting to emotional appeals, slander or personal attacks against political opponents. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said campaigning should centre on explaining the agenda for the people and the state government's achievements over the past four years. Also present was incumbent Taboh Naning assemblyman Datuk Zulkiflee Mohd Zin.

items.title: Campaign ‘flag war’ begins in Melaka as parties stretch limited election budgets
items.summary: Several political parties are reusing flags from previous state elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan for the Melaka polls. Political party flags line the roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. Political party flags are being put up along roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026.

items.title: Ab Rauf: Melaka voters, not political rivals, will judge state govt's performance
items.summary: MELAKA: Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh maintains that the state government's performance should be measured and judged by the people, not its political rivals. I believe the people of Melaka know what we have done. Earlier, Adly had questioned the performance of the BN-led Melaka government despite securing a strong mandate by winning 21 of the 28 seats in the previous state election.

items.title: Shahrizat says BN reps must serve beyond election periods
items.summary: KOTA MELAKA: Veteran Umno leader Tan Sri Shahrizat Abdul Jalil has called on Barisan Nasional (BN) representatives to continue serving their constituents between elections, citing Duyong incumbent Mohd Noor Helmy as an example. Shahrizat, an Umno Supreme Council member, said Mohd Noor Helmy remained accessible to residents and continued addressing their concerns throughout his term. Also present were Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis, and BN candidate Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem.

items.title: Fahmi: Three more Asean countries keen to join Malaysia-led children’s online safety push
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Thailand, Brunei and Cambodia are the latest Asean countries to have expressed interest in joining Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore in efforts to address online safety issues involving children. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he welcomed the development, describing it as a sign that Asean was moving in the same direction. Also present was Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.

items.title: BN banks on five-year track record to win fence-sitters at Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is confident that the achievements and performance of the state administration over the past five years will be among the key factors considered by fence-sitters in determining their choice of candidate in the Melaka state election on November 14. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said these voters would assess the party based on its ability to administer the state, as well as the effectiveness of policies and initiatives that directly benefit the people. Ab Rauf, who is also Chief Minister, said approaches taken by the state government to win over the group included the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR), Hari Exco Bertemu Rakyat and Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programmes, which focus on identifying and resolving various issues faced by the people.

items.title: Klang's Little India bustling despite rain ahead of Deepavali
items.summary: KLANG: Hindu shoppers are braving the rain to finish their Deepavali shopping at Klang's Little India ahead of the celebrations on Nov 8. Engineer S. Meiyarasan, 28, said his family had opted for last-minute shopping while keeping an eye on Klang's weather, which usually brings afternoon downpours. "This helps ensure our shopping trip for festive essentials, especially clothes and food, goes smoothly.

items.title: BN began engaging voters long before Melaka polls, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA: The first day of campaigning for the 16th Melaka election was relatively calmer than previous elections, says Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. He attributed this to BN's early efforts to engage with the people, rather than limiting its outreach to the 14-day campaign period. "Therefore, we must regard the position of an elected representative as a trust to serve the people, not for the people to serve us," he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: MCMC won’t interfere in parties’ social media campaigns, will only act on complaints
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by contesting political parties during the 16th Melaka State Election, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts concerning campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms,” he said when asked about MCMC’s online monitoring measures during the Melaka polls scheduled for November 14. Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC is also monitoring the misuse of social media accounts to spread false information, the use of deepfakes, and extremely offensive content.

items.title: Nga: Housing must put people and communities first
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Housing development must prioritise affordability, liveability and community well-being rather than treating homes as commercial commodities, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said. Nga, who is also president of the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) Assembly, said urban progress should not be measured solely by the number of skyscrapers, but by improvements in community well-being. Nga said meeting these benchmarks required coordinated action by governments, builders, developers and the wider community.

items.title: Thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India's capital on Sunday, renewing demands for the country's election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party. The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month. The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

items.title: With no majority, what options remain for Israel's Netanyahu, Eisenkot?
items.summary: FOLLOWING elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot both fell short of a majority, each is claiming a mandate to govern – though neither has explained how. A Netanyahu-led government The prime minister and his far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies came out ahead in the final vote count, with 53 seats in parliament, including 27 for the premier's party, Likud. Of the four parties in Eisenkot's camp, the least receptive to an overture from Netanyahu would be the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, which won eight seats.

items.title: Zahid: BN ready to invite PN to join state gov't if it wins Melaka polls
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK: Barisan Nasional is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government following the 16th Melaka election on Nov 14. "As happened in Negri Sembilan, when the government was formed, we honoured the appointments to ensure that they (PN) were part of the government. The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on Nov 10.

items.title: Anwar among racing buffs in Sepang to watch Marquez win Malaysian MotoGP
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today spent time watching the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here. Today’s race saw Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez strengthen his position at the summit of the 2026 MotoGP world championship after emerging as the champion, followed by Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in second place and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP in third. The victory saw Marc Marquez collect 399 points, thereby widening the gap to 44 points over his closest challenger, Jorge Martin of Aprilia Racing, who now has 355 points.

items.title: Azalina: All 218 MPs get a role in reforms under CSA as AG-PP split, PM term limit need cross-party support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Cross-party cooperation through the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) is important in building parliamentary consensus to advance institutional reforms in the country, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. In this regard, she welcomed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s support for the implementation of the CSA, as well as his proposal to extend the cooperation to more opposition parties. Azalina said that as part of the Unity Government, Barisan Nasional (BN) would continue to play a constructive role in maintaining political stability, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring the country’s administration functions effectively in the interests of the people.

items.title: Zahid: Rural and Regional Development Ministry aims to clear RM259.5m in project arrears by year-end
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes that outstanding payments for projects under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) can be resolved amicably by the end of this year. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts would be made to ensure payments for completed projects that had yet to be settled, including progress payments due to contractors and suppliers, could be made. “We will endeavour to ensure that funds are made available to settle payments for projects that have been completed but remain unpaid, as well as progress payments due to contractors and suppliers.

items.title: BN ready to invite Perikatan to join state govt if it wins Melaka polls, says Zahid
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional (PN) to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026 .

items.title: Four dead as cars veer into oncoming lanes in separate KL, Johor crashes
items.summary: In an accident involving a Perodua Myvi and a Toyota Vellfire at Kilometer 23 of the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2), near Bukit Antarabangsa, early this morning, two men were killed. He said the Vellfire driver and a passenger were also injured and rushed to Ampang Hospital; however, the driver was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at the hospital, while the passenger remains hospitalised. Kulai district police chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the accident involving a Toyota Vios and a Mazda at about 2.30pm.

items.title: Sarawak explores collaboration with Russia on rocket, satellite launches, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 1 — The Sarawak government is exploring potential collaboration with Russia in rocket and satellite launches, leveraging the state’s strategic location near the Equator. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the proposal was raised by the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Malaysia, Naiyl M. Latypov, during a courtesy call last week. Abang Johari said Sarawak must capitalise on growing international interest in the state by implementing effective policies and ensuring clear development plans.

items.title: AGC files appeal, weighs bid to reinstate murder charge against senior Perak cop in student hit-and-run case
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is considering whether to seek the reinstatement of a murder charge against a senior police officer in the case involving the death of student Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie, following the officer’s conviction on a lesser charge of causing death. Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the AGC had filed an appeal at the Court of Appeal last week against the Ipoh High Court’s decision, but was still examining the various aspects of the case before deciding on the arguments to be submitted. On October 28, the Ipoh High Court sentenced DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, 47, to seven years and six months’ imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to an amended charge of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, three years ago.

items.title: Immigration Dept: Report special pass irregularities directly to us or MACC
items.summary: Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said information or evidence could be submitted to JIM or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to facilitate a comprehensive investigation. “Providing information directly to the authorities is crucial to protecting the confidentiality of information and preserving the integrity of evidence. Zakaria said JIM welcomed information on alleged misconduct by its officers and would ensure that all reports received were reviewed and referred for appropriate action under the prevailing laws and regulations.

items.title: Brace for the toughest GE yet: Loke warns DAP as BN and Perikatan close ranks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP must prepare for its toughest general election yet as growing cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) threatens to upend the country’s political landscape, Anthony Loke said today. Addressing delegates at the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territories DAP annual convention today, Loke urged members to cast aside complacency and tighten the party’s machinery ahead of the 16th general election (GE16). DAP’s core objective in Kuala Lumpur remains retaining all five parliamentary seats secured during the 15th general election (GE15).

items.title: Malaysia ranked 12th of 163 in 2026 Global Peace Index, reflecting security efforts, says Saifuddin Nasution
items.summary: RAUB, Nov 1 — Malaysia’s 12th-place ranking among 163 countries in the 2026 Global Peace Index (GPI) reflects the country’s ongoing efforts to maintain safety and security, particularly through the work of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution said the IPCC played an important role in ensuring that the police force continued to uphold high standards in carrying out its duties. Saifuddin Nasution said the IPCC played an important role in ensuring that the police force continued to uphold high standards in carrying out its duties.

items.title: Anwar: Manage govt funds with care or face arrest, charges
items.summary: KAJANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that government funds must be properly safeguarded and managed, warning that strict action would be taken against anyone who betrayed the trust placed in them. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said agencies providing financing for entrepreneurship, including the National Entrepreneurial Group Economic Fund (TEKUN Nasional), Bank Rakyat and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), bore a major responsibility to ensure funds reached their intended beneficiaries without leakage or misappropriation. “Manage these funds properly...

items.title: Foster healthy lifestyles: Nearly two million Malaysians benefit from 38 Wellness Hubs nationwide, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Nearly two million people have benefited from 38 Wellness Hub facilities operating nationwide under the Ministry of Health’s (MOH) initiative to expand access to disease prevention and foster healthy lifestyles. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said two of these facilities are located in Melaka, namely in Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah, serving as community wellness referral centres. At Wellness Hubs, we offer weight management services (IFitEr), smoking cessation support, mental health screenings, the ‘Stay Active’ module, and exercise therapy,” he said.

items.title: Zahid: Govt on alert, ramps up readiness as El Nino raises monsoon flood risks
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — The government and all relevant agencies are fully prepared to face the North-east Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to have a more severe impact than in previous years. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the state of preparedness involved comprehensive coordination between the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and disaster management committees at state and district levels, following the launch of National Preparedness Month 2026 in Ipoh last month. Asked whether certain states would be the main focus during the monsoon season, Ahmad Zahid said Kelantan, Terengganu, the northern states, particularly Kedah, as well as southern states comprising Johor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan were frequently affected by the North-east Monsoon.

items.title: Adly Zahari to be Pakatan’s chief minister candidate if coalition wins Melaka
items.summary: KAJANG, Nov 1 — Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari will be named Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) candidate for Chief Minister if the coalition succeeds in forming the state government following the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. PH Election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Adly, a former Melaka Chief Minister, was the best candidate for the position. “Adly is the best candidate (for Chief Minister), along with a few others.

items.title: Sepang circuit must be more than just a race track: Deputy minister pushes for serious F1 evaluation
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 1 — The possibility of bringing Formula 1 (F1) racing back to Malaysia must be seriously evaluated, while the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) must be strengthened as a strategic national asset, says Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Aiman Athirah Sabu. “SIC is not merely a racing circuit. She said SIC needed to diversify its revenue streams through corporate sponsorships, commercial rights, hospitality packages, facility rentals, additional events and strategic partnerships with automotive manufacturers and international industry partners.

items.title: Pakatan tells its supporters in Melaka: Vote with your conscience
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is taking an open approach and leaving it to its members and supporters to decide whom to support in state seats not contested by the coalition in the 16th Melaka state election. He said PH’s current focus was on securing victory in the 24 state seats contested by the coalition. Asked about Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia’s (Bersatu) decision to contest eight state seats, Adly said the party had its own plans for the Melaka state election.

items.title: Anwar pledges RM1m boost for hawkers and urges an end to tedious loan paperwork
items.summary: KAJANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced an allocation of RM1 million to the Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (KUSKOP) to coordinate assistance for associations, hawkers, and small traders to boost their income. He said the allocation takes into account the hundreds of thousands of hawkers, small traders, and associations operating nationwide. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the allocation channelled to associations, hawkers, and small traders would help improve family incomes.

items.title: Najib still to pay RM50m fine needed for house arrest, says AG
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to pay his RM50 million fine, according to the latest information received by the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC). The order was conditional upon Najib paying the RM50 million fine. In July 2020, the Kuala Lumpur High Court sentenced Najib to 12 years’ imprisonment and fined him RM210 million after finding him guilty of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

items.title: DAP urges government to make Najib’s pardon board minutes public
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to release the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting regarding former prime minister Najib Razak’s conditional pardon. Speaking earlier at the Federal Territories DAP convention, Loke acknowledged that Najib’s conditional pardon has sparked significant public questioning. He said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, a board member, had clearly communicated the party’s stance against house arrest for those involved in major corruption scandals.

items.title: No registration needed: STR recipients 40 and above automatically qualify for PeKa Sihat, says Teo Nie Ching
items.summary: KULAI, Nov 1 — Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients aged 40 and above are urged to make full use of the PeKa Sihat (Healthcare Scheme for the B40 Group) initiative, which offers various free health screenings and treatments starting next year following an RM80 million government allocation. She noted that a key benefit of the initiative is free health screenings at private clinics to detect conditions such as diabetes and high cholesterol, thereby easing congestion at government health facilities. Administered by ProtectHealth, PeKa Sihat is a government healthcare initiative aimed at encouraging eligible Malaysians to undergo health screenings and identify health risks early.

items.title: Puchong plant processes 40,000 chickens daily, used stunning voltage up to 13 times halal limit, say police
items.summary: PUCHONG, Nov 1 — A chicken processing plant in Kampung Sri Aman Hilir here, raided during Op Taring Chiller, is believed to have the capacity to process more than 40,000 chickens a day, while allegedly using electrical voltage far exceeding the prescribed limit for the slaughtering method. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) deputy director (Operations) Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said preliminary investigations found that the live chickens were sourced from Sungai Sepat, Sungai Pelek and Sepang before being processed at the plant. Commenting on the water-bath stunning method used at the plant, Muhammad said investigations found that the premises had allegedly used electrical voltage exceeding the prescribed limit, resulting in the chickens dying before the slaughtering process.
